children: The acquisition gives Prestige Estates complete ownership of Allure Developers and its ongoing residential project in Noida

Prestige Estates Projects has acquired a 100 per cent stake in Allure Developers Pvt Ltd for Rs 523.76 crore, strengthening its residential portfolio in the Delhi-NCR market. The acquisition gives the Bengaluru-based real estate developer control of a residential project being developed in Noida's Sector 150.

The company entered into a share purchase agreement on November 6, 2026, to acquire the entire equity share capital of Allure Developers, according to a regulatory filing. Following the transaction, Allure Developers has become a wholly owned subsidiary of Prestige Estates, with the consideration to be paid in tranches.

The acquisition is part of Prestige Estates' expansion strategy and adds to its recent investments across different real estate segments. The company has been pursuing acquisitions to expand its development portfolio and strengthen its presence in key property markets.

The latest transaction follows Prestige Estates' acquisition of 100 per cent equity in Gloind Vintage Infra for an enterprise value of Rs 519 crore. The deal was executed through its subsidiary, Prestige Retail Ventures, as part of the group's investment activity.

Upon completion, Prestige Estates will indirectly hold the entire equity share capital of Gloind Vintage Infra. The transaction will also give it indirect ownership and control of Tarun Realtors, a subsidiary of Gloind that owns a shopping mall in Bengaluru.

The acquisitions come against the backdrop of a decline in the company's financial performance during the September quarter. Prestige Estates reported a 44 per cent year-on-year fall in consolidated net profit to Rs 256.2 crore for the quarter, compared with Rs 457.4 crore in the corresponding period last year.

The company's total income also declined during the quarter, falling to Rs 2,222.2 crore from Rs 2,697.8 crore in the year-ago period, according to the regulatory filing. The decline in both profit and income reflects the company's performance during the second quarter of the current financial year.

For the April-September period, consolidated net profit fell to Rs 527.6 crore from Rs 768.9 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. Total income during the first half also declined to Rs 5,057.8 crore from Rs 5,166.5 crore a year earlier.
